advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'local_id property read failed' from 'property absent' so a failed enrichment read does not silently re-enable duplicate creates (e.g. mark keys whose read errored so downstream stands down conservatively or surfaces an alert).
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetch_paging.py:85 `except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — fail-open enrichment; never break fetch` then `continue`
fetch_paging.py:75-84 the HTTPError branch also `continue`s on any non-404 code after logging

Downstream consumers key only on presence: fetch_paging effect is consumed by binding_walk.py:354 `claimed_local_id = fields.get("local_id")`, differ.py:540 `if jira_local_id_str in local_rebar_ids`, reconcile_helpers.py:214 `bool(fields.get("local_id"))`, outbound_mutation_builders.py:118 `remote_fields.get("local_id")`
ABSENCE rationale: none of these consumers can distinguish 'property read failed' from 'property not set' — the suppression verdict collapses to the enrichment's own failure mode
advisory.finding: The local_id enrichment fails open: a non-404 read failure (transport 5xx, timeout, malformed body) is logged and skipped, leaving fields['local_id'] absent — which is indistinguishable to every downstream suppressor (binding_walk _skip_unbound_adopt, differ local_rebar_ids gate, drop_snapshot_differ_property_bound_emissions, outbound builder scan) from 'this issue genuinely has no local_id property'. When the read fails, the dedup the change is designed to enforce silently does not fire and the duplicate create reappears, with only a warning log distinguishing the two worlds.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Avoid per-issue `get_issue_property` fan-out in `enrich_local_id_properties`; restrict the property read to the small set of issues actually needing identity recovery (or batch it), so fetch cost does not scale O(N) with snapshot size.
evidence: fetch_paging.py:70-74: `for issue_key, fields in snapshot.items(): ... local_id = get_property(issue_key, "local_id")`
fetch_paging.py:62 docstring: "The base search payload does not include issue properties." — so `fields.get("local_id")` (line 71) is falsy for nearly every entry, defeating the short-circuit
acli_rest.py:277-278: `path = f"/rest/api/3/issue/{jira_key}/properties/{property_key}"; response = self._direct_rest_get(path)` — get_issue_property is a synchronous per-issue REST GET
fetcher.py:599: `enrich_local_id_properties(client, snapshot, _fetcher_log)` invoked once per full snapshot build
fetcher.py: `_DONE_RECENT_CAP = 1000` — snapshot bounds Done issues at 1000, plus all active issues, so N is on the order of thousands
advisory.finding: `enrich_local_id_properties` issues one synchronous `get_issue_property` REST call per snapshot issue that lacks a `local_id` field — an N+1 remote-call-in-a-loop. Because the base search payload never includes the property (per the function's own docstring), the `fields.get('local_id')` guard short-circuits almost nothing, so the number of round-trips scales linearly with the Jira snapshot size (active issues + up to 1000 Done issues), on every fetch pass.
scenarios: A Jira project with hundreds/thousands of issues: the fetch now performs one extra REST GET per issue, adding thousands of serial round-trips to every reconcile pass
Large steady-state snapshots where most issues have no in-payload local_id, so the guard never skips the remote call
